scope: Independent read-only review of the exact proposed archive-copy deletion and same-filesystem hardlink coalescing plan, stored cloud snapshots, actual local retained archive bytes, and frozen replay contract. No cloud operation or image inspection was performed.
decision_reasons: The verified plan selects exactly 204 transfer-archive files with exact retained local archive backups and holds the single unmatched archive. Current local retained backup files are independently rehashed and their sizes/hashes match the recorded cloud archive hashes; archive contents were not opened.

The 2,764 replay-media paths consist of 691 images, 691 alpha masks, 691 guides and 691 overviews. Each is a separate regular file in the stored pre-cleanup snapshot, on the same device as its byte-identical canonical counterpart. Proposed deletion, replay replacement, canonical retention and held-path sets are disjoint, and reclaim accounting does not double count an inode.

verify_extraction_replay checks historical zero-network replay identity/timing, matching native and output hashes/geometry, and separately resolved output pathnames. It does not require different current st_dev/st_ino or use Path.samefile. A hardlink keeps two different resolved pathnames while sharing an inode, so exact original pathnames and all receipt/file byte bindings can remain valid.

verify_extracted_image checks geometry, SHA-256, image/mask format/dimensions/decodability and alpha coverage. Byte-identical hardlinks preserve those values. Coalescing after an actual independently executed and separately persisted historical replay is a storage representation change, not a replacement for that replay execution or for source-pixel reconstruction.

All JSON, logs, replay/binding receipts, source-range files, canonical media, source/core snapshots, runtime files and other projects remain outside the operation allowlists. The unchanged JSON execution times remain historical evidence. This review supports a conditional plan, not completed cleanup, durable backup independence, model quality or WP-P6-01 closure.

The immutable clarification note binds this exact plan SHA and explicitly states shared-inode metadata adoption, historical-replay versus physical-backup scope, immutability and the archive-only option. It resolves the filesystem-metadata wording without changing the plan or its targets.

held_files.reason: No verified exact local archive backup; retain.

checks.filename_contract_check: Exact approved plan pathname plus same-basename canonical mapping and media category/extension; no invented bounded-extract-only prefix requirement.

contract_references.purpose: Rooted file path, actual SHA and stat-keyed per-audit cache
Stored JPEG/mask bytes and geometry checks
Historical independently persisted replay, byte identity and distinct output pathnames
Path.resolve normalizes path/symlinks, not hardlink inode aliases
Independent cache-only replay outputs and actual source reconstruction remain required

required_before_apply: Obtain explicit user approval for this exact plan SHA and its deletion plus hardlink scope. This audit is not approval, and no deletion or coalescing is currently authorized by it.

Acquire the existing project lock, take fresh disk/resource/container/service snapshots, establish no active P6 writers or open users of affected files, and keep frozen canonical and replay media immutable for the whole operation. Stored /proc observations are a point-in-time best effort and do not replace this check.

Revalidate every approved source/target and retained canonical path with lstat and realpath containment, no symlink redirection in any ancestor, correct regular-file type, exact path/size/hash and expected device/inode/nlink. Refuse changed files rather than widening the allowlist. Check local retained archive backups again immediately before remote archive deletion.

For hardlinks, freshly confirm both endpoints share a filesystem and that canonical owner/mode/ACL/xattrs allow the expected readers. The plan snapshots do not record all of those attributes. Do not chmod or utime a shared inode merely to imitate the old replay inode; abort any incompatible case.

Preserve each replay receipt, binding and historical execution record byte-for-byte. Independent replay must have actually executed and persisted separately before coalescing; hardlinks must never be used to fabricate or skip that execution.

Create a unique sibling temporary hardlink from the retained canonical inode, validate that link, then atomically replace only its approved replay pathname. Never unlink the original replay pathname first, never modify canonical content, never fall back to symlinks, rewriting JSON, source synthesis or unplanned copies. Persist per-file intent/result records and use durable directory updates where supported.

Delete only the approved 204 exact regular archive pathnames after confirming retained local backups. Keep the unmatched tar and every unlisted pathname. If checks fail or a lock/user appears, stop without expanding the cleanup scope.
Satisfy applier review findings A1-A4 and bind the final reviewed executor revision. supports_plan is the metadata/contract decision; it does not mark the current executor ready to apply.
required_after_apply: Use a fresh verification process/cache. Recheck every hardlinked replay pathname and its canonical pathname: both exist as regular files, original SHA and size remain, resolved pathnames stay distinct, and st_dev/st_ino match. With the approved one-to-one nlink=1 baseline, each canonical/replay pair should have nlink=2 unless an explicitly recorded extra link exists; unexpected links or partial operations require investigation.

Confirm only the 204 approved archive names are absent and that all exact local backups and the held archive still exist with matching hashes. Preserve JSON/log/receipt/binding/source-range paths and their pre-operation bytes; canonical data and all unlisted service/project files must remain unchanged.

Rerun the actual integrated six-observation frozen core source/byte audit and compare its per-case issues against the exact pre-cleanup baseline, plus revalidate all 2,764 changed replay byte bindings. The integrated run is expected to remain missing overall; a clean storage operation does not close the business gate.

Record actual per-file operations and before/after filesystem free space and allocated-byte measurements. The 12.493984 GiB total is a snapshot estimate, not a guaranteed release; open handles, snapshots/filesystem accounting and concurrent activity may change the measured result.

Compare container/service/resource snapshots and verify other projects are unchanged. Preserve partial-operation/crash records and any temporary-link state for controlled recovery; never report all-or-nothing success without per-file completion evidence.
limitations_and_disclosure: This audit rehashes local backups and checks saved cloud snapshots; it does not independently rehash current live remote bytes, survey every possible external dependency or execute the plan. All current cloud checks remain pre-apply requirements.

The hardlinked paths cease to be independent physical backup copies. Future in-place writes through either pathname affect both; later extractions or edits must use new independent output paths or explicitly materialize separate copies first. Historical separate replay execution remains evidence and must not be relabeled as a newly independent physical copy.

All 2,764 replay files have different pre-operation mtimes from their canonical files. Hardlinks necessarily change replay inode/link count/ctime and expose canonical mtime/ownership/mode/xattrs; therefore keeping metadata means preserving evidence JSON and historical timestamps, not preserving every original filesystem attribute. No blanket filesystem-metadata-unchanged claim is supported.

The contract review concerns continued frozen pathname/hash/geometry compatibility. It does not newly prove each historical replay execution, independent human truth, dataset admission or model quality. Existing source replays still require real source bytes and actual decoding at their gate.

Exact local transfer archives provide retained bytes outside the cloud copy, not an independently tested disaster-recovery guarantee. Current paths are checked without opening archive members or images.

draft_correction.reason: The first audit draft incorrectly imposed a bounded-extract filename prefix. The frozen storage contract and exact approved plan also include reserve-extract and addendum-extract. All 160 false-positive entries were rechecked against the exact plan, original inventory, byte matches and same-basename canonical mapping. No input plan or original evidence was changed.

applier_review.scope: Static review of user-approval gating, exact whitelist, existing lock, byte revalidation, atomic replacement, per-file accounting and post-core verification. Not executed by this auditor.
confirmed: Default dry-run exits before creating an output directory or contacting cloud.
Apply requires an actual approval file bound to exact plan, notes and audit digests and the authorized mode.
The existing stack.lock is opened read-only and flocked exclusively, with no global lock/config modification.
Remote preflight checks exact target stat/hash, contained regular paths, retained canonical byte equality and same filesystem, no current P6 users and no running container mounting the cleanup root.
Replacement uses sibling os.link followed by os.replace; archive deletes are confined to approved setup/transfer names.
The frozen integrated six-observation source core is rerun under exact code/input hashes, and business status remains missing.

findings.issue: Operations are logged only after rename/unlink, and log.flush without fsync leaves a crash window in which changes or staged links can exist without a durable per-file record.
findings.required_change: Write and fsync per-file intent including source/target/staged path before mutation, persist completion after mutation, and durably update directories where supported. Preserve partial or pending intent state for recovery.

findings.issue: The post-core command return code is recorded but not required to be zero. Only missing status and absence of sample/pair issues are compared; new global issues can be missed.
findings.required_change: Require returncode == 0 and compare the deterministic full core result or complete issues/issue_counts and identity counters against the exact bound baseline.

findings.issue: Per-item replacement checks do not provide a final whole-whitelist check of every hardlink, deleted archive and held archive.
findings.required_change: Before completed status, rehash/restat every approved replay/canonical pair, verify regular distinct resolved pathnames with shared device/inode and expected links, confirm every approved archive absent, and verify held archive plus protected evidence unchanged.

findings.issue: Canonical/staged safety is not rechecked via lstat/realpath immediately around each operation, and owner/mode compatibility is not recorded.
findings.required_change: Revalidate canonical/target/staged containment and regular-file identity around link/replace, record owner/mode metadata and refuse incompatible access changes; never copy old replay metadata onto a shared inode.
